questions.question: Give an account on a method of growing microscopic organisms in a medium to feed fish fry and larvae / [CO1, CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Give an account of a method of growing microscopic organisms in a medium to feed fish fry
  • andlarvae. [U]/[CO1,CO4]
  • i. Algae: minute floating, aquatic plant-like organisms.
  • Groundnut oil cake, urea, and superphosphate are mixed and diluted in water and added to
  • cement tanks along with algae from a stock culture. The algae are collected and fed to the fish
  • larvae.
  • ii. Rotifers: free-swimming minute organisms in seawater known as 'wheel animalcules'.
  • Filtered seawater, urea and superphosphate are added to the water, along with the stock
  • culture of chlorella. A stock culture of rotifers is added to this mixture on the next day.
  • Salinity (30ppt) and temperature (25-35°C). In 6-7 days, rotifers multiply and increase in
  • concentration.
  • iii. Moina: free-floating minute organisms belonging to a group of animals known as cladocerans.
  • Filtered seawater, urea and superphosphate are added to the water, along with the stock
  • culture of chlorella. Moina stock culture is added to it. In 5-7 days, Moina cell density
  • increases.
  • iv. Daphnia: floating animals belong to the cladocerans.
  • Pond water is manured with chicken droppings, oil cakes and superphosphate, and in a few
  • days the water turns green, indicating growth of plankton. Daphnia is introduced to it. Liquid
  • manure is added to the tank daily.
  • v. Infusoria: the smallest of all live feeds for fish larvae
  • Water is taken in a tank, and banana peel, cabbage leaves or potato pieces are added and left
  • in the shade. Medium for infusoria can also be developed by using aquatic plants, skimmed
  • milk, etc. The medium is covered by a velon screen and kept for bacterial development.
  • Decaying vegetation acts as food for the bacteria; the infusoria feed on these bacteria and
  • multiply.
  • vi. Earthworm: found in moist and loose soils. They are washed to remove the adhering soil and
  • killed by pouring hot water or kept in live conditions.
  • vii. Mosquito larvae: collected from stagnant pools of dirty water and cultured. Take water in a
  • bucket, add cow dung or decaying leaves and keep undisturbed in a place away from sunlight
  • and fresh air. Mosquitoes lay eggs in the water; the larvae can be collected by a sieve and
  • given to fish.
  • viii. Artemia: also known as brine shrimp, inhabit salt pans of high salinity.
  • The cysts are put in saline water (1-5 g/l) at a temperature of 27-30°C and aerated for 24-26
  • hours. When they hatch out, aeration can be stopped and the larvae can be attracted by a light
  • source and siphoned off from the jar, washed and given to the fish as live feed.
  • (Any 2 points with short description )

questions.question: Describe the breeding habits of Gourami. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• DescribethebreedinghabitsofGourami. [U]/[CO1]
  • Gouramis are one of the popular aquarium species, being bubble-nesters, where the male builds a
  • nest of bubbles for eggs, which he then guards. During courtship, the male and female care for
  • eachother; themalenudgesthefemaleintoapositionbeneaththenest. The male curves his body
  • around the female and tips her over so that her abdomen is directed towards the nest. Spawning lasts
  • for several hours. Eggs are light and float upon release. The male carefully gathers any stragglers
  • and places them back in the nest.Oncethefryhatches,themaleshouldberemoved.
  • (Liberal valuation)

questions.question: Discuss the importance of water quality monitoring in feeding management. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Discusstheimportanceofwaterqualitymonitoringinfeedingmanagement. [K]/[CO1]
  • Water quality monitoring is crucial for feeding management because it directly impactsanimalhealth,
  • disease resistance, feed efficiency, and the quality of the aquatic life. By regularly monitoring
  • parameters like dissolved oxygen, pH, temperature, hardness, turbidity, salinity, and alkalinity,
  • aquarium keepers can prevent disease, optimise feeding strategies, and ensure that the water used in
  • processing doesn't contaminate the food. This proactive approach is essential for maximising
  • productivity and minimising costs associated with poor water quality.

questions.question: Write an account on the importance of water quality and environmental stability in the breeding success of bettas, and discuss best practices for maintaining these conditions. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Write an account on the importance of water quality and environmental stability in the
  • breeding success of bettas, and discuss best practices for maintaining these conditions. [A] /
  • [CO3]
  • The Siamese fighting fish, Betta splendens, are known for their brilliant colours, large flowing fins
  • and their peculiar territorial behaviour. They exhibit parental care and bubble nest-building behaviour.
  • Bettas are sensitive to fluctuations in their environment, and stable water parameters are essential for
  • stimulating spawning behaviour and ensuring the survival of eggs and fry. For broodstock
  • development, the males and females are grown in separate tanks upon attaining maturity.
  • Broodstock is then taken to50Lbreedingtanks,spaciousenough for the males to chase the females.

questions.question: Explain the breeding technique of goldfish.
questions.solution_html:
• Explainthebreedingtechniqueofgoldfish. ( Liberal Valuation)
  • Gold fishes are egg scatterers with no parental care. Females lay 5,000–15,000 adhesive
  • eggs. Males have white spots on operculum and fins and females have soft, swollen
  • abdomens. When mature male releases milt. 50% of water in the breeding tanks are replaced
  • daily, two weeks before breeding. Males and females for breeding purpose are generally
  • placed in smaller tanks with aquatic plants or materials (e.g., nylon fibers) for egg adhesion.
  • Males stimulate females during courtship to release eggs.Fertilized eggs are translucent;
  • unfertilized eggs turn white. Eggs hatch in 48–72 hours. After eggs are hatched breeders are
  • removed to prevent egg consumption. No feed are given for 3 days. After 3 days live feed
  • like infusoria, brine shrimp or boiled egg yolk. Are given to the growing fish fry.
  • (Anyrelevantpoints-4marks)

questions.question: How do guppies, mollies, and swordtails differ in their approaches to caring for their fry? / [CO3]

  • feeding. Live food includes baby brine shrimp, microworms, Daphnia, and hard-boiled egg yolk paste
  • can be given as a protein-rich alternative for live feeds.Fryrequiresfrequentfeeding (5 times a day.)

  • parents. The fry can be fedwith artificial feed in the form of flakes; newlyhatched brine shrimp
  • provides a more wholesome live feed. The combination of Spirulina algae and brine shrimp is

questions.question: Illustrate the role of the nitrogen cycle in an aquarium.
questions.solution_html:
• Illustrate the role of the nitrogen cycle in an aquarium. (Out of Syllabus - Give full
  • marks if attempted)
  • The nitrogen cycle ensures the breakdown of harmful waste products in an aquarium.
  • Fish excreta and decaying organic matter produce ammonia (toxic). Beneficial bacteria
  • (Nitrosomonas) convert ammonia into nitrites (less toxic). Another bacterial group
  • (Nitrobacter) converts nitrites into nitrates (relatively harmless). Plants absorb nitrates
  • synthesize aminoacids, organic compounds.
  • Significance: Maintains water quality, prevents ammonia toxicity and ensures a healthy
  • environment for fish and plants.

questions.question: Give an account on the sex identification features and broodstock maintenance of swordtail fish. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Give an account of the sex identification features and broodstock maintenance of swordtail
  • fish. [S]/[CO3]
  • Swordtail is one of the most popular aquarium fish of the family Poeciliidae. Swordtails are mild in
  • behaviour and can be housed in a community aquarium.
  • Sex identification: Adult males and females can be easily differentiated. Females are larger in size
  • than the males and have much more rounded bellies. Males are thinner, elongated and develop a
  • distinctsword-likeelongationofthelowerlobeoftheirtailfin as they mature, butfemalesdonot
  • have an elongated lower lobe for the caudal fin. Mature males exhibit a distinct male sex organ
  • called a gonopodium (modification of the anal fin), which is used as a copulatory organ for
  • depositingspermintothefemaleduringmating.
  • Maintenance of broodstock: Swordtail should be provided with plenty of room to swim and may
  • require one square foot per individual fish. The tank bottom should contain a substrate of fine sand or
  • smooth gravel. They prefer a warmer temperature range of 21-27°C, with 24°C as the optimum.
  • The pH should be maintained at 7-8.4. Floating plants should be provided in the tank for the
  • young to hide, as they exhibit cannibalism. The water has to be kept well aerated and heavily
  • planted to prevent the fish from jumping out. Males and females of desirable body shape and colour
  • are selected as the broodstock. Swordtail can be kept in sets of 3-4 females per male. Minimum
  • feedingisrequired as they feed on detritus and algae. Frozen foods like brine shrimps, krill, Daphnia,
  • and plankton can also be given.
  • (Sex identification features – 2 marks; Broodstock maintenance – 2 marks)

questions.question: Analyze the importance of filtration systems in maintaining a healthy aquarium environment. (5 × 4 = 20) END OF THE QUESTION PAPER ***
questions.solution_html:
• Analyze the importance of filtration systems in maintaining a healthy aquarium
  • environment.(Liberal valuation )
  • Filtration systems are critical for maintaining a healthy aquarium environment, ensuring the
  • well-being of aquatic organisms, and promoting sustainable aquarium management.
  • Filtration systems effectively remove physical, chemical, and biological contaminants,
  • ensuring clear and clean water. This supports the stability of water parameters. Mechanical
  • filtration reduces particulate matter, preventing gill damage and respiratory issues in fish.
  • Biological filtration converts toxic substances like ammonia and nitrite into less harmful
  • nitrate, reducing stress and promoting fish health. By eliminating debris and organic
  • particles that can harbor harmful microorganisms, filtration systems lower the risk of disease
  • outbreaks, ensuring the aquarium remains a safe environment for the fishes. Clean water
  • conditions promote better feed conversion, faster growth rates, and improved overall health
  • of aquatic species. Filtration systems reduces the need for frequent water changes and
  • minimizes the environmental impact of waste disposal.
  • (Anyrelevantpoints-4marks)
